page.summary: Read the pallet route, spend a drop only when it buys a useful next position, and reset a safe dropped pallet when the recovery repays its time.

verdict.recommendation: Manage pallets as a team resource: identify the next route before dropping, and do not turn information or reset tools into reasons to spend a pallet without chase value.
verdict.soloQ: Use pallet information to avoid dead zones, then make the drop and reset decision yourself; return to objectives when the route is gone.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Call which pallet area is being spent and whether a reset is safe so teammates do not duplicate the same resource trip.
verdict.mainWeakness: Map RNG, fast resource destruction, cooldowns and a Killer who changes timing can remove the expected pallet economy.

plans.label: Pallet resource module
plans.why: The source defines a pallet-economy framework, not a verified four-perk build. These tools cover route reading, reset value and a Killer-position cue without claiming a complete recipe.

choices.whyItsHere: When Terror Radius or chase conditions are active, read nearby Pallets and use the post-drop movement to leave toward the next route.
Make a reset decision for a dropped pallet only when the interaction is safe and the restored route will matter to the team.
Use a Break or Damage aura reveal to decide whether the Killer is clearing your route or has moved away; it does not reveal every pallet.

opening: While approaching a chase area, identify one pallet that buys the next position and one exit from the tile. Reserve the resource for a route-changing drop rather than spending it to prove the build is active.

rows.situation: You are inside the conditions for Five Moves Ahead and need a pallet route.
rows.action: Choose the closest pallet that leads to a real next position, then keep the exit in mind before taking the interaction.
rows.why: The perk supplies pallet information during its active conditions; the value is route selection, not a reason to drop immediately.

rows.situation: The Killer reaches a pallet and the drop can create distance or protect the next objective route.
rows.action: Drop only when the resulting distance or denial is worth the resource. Move through the planned exit and reassess after the perk cooldown begins.
rows.why: A pallet spent only for an aura or movement trigger leaves the team with less future safety.

rows.situation: A dropped pallet is useful again and Any Means Necessary can be completed without giving the Killer a free hit.
rows.action: Reset it only after checking the Killer's location and the team's next route. If the interaction is contested, leave and keep the objective moving.
rows.why: Resetting restores a resource only when the time and exposure do not cost more than the pallet returns.

rows.situation: The Killer breaks or damages a pallet, and Alert reveals the Killer's Aura.
rows.action: Use the aura cue to update the route and tell teammates which resource is being removed. Do not interpret it as a pallet or window map.
rows.why: Alert reports Killer Break or Damage actions; the information is useful because it changes resource state.

rows.situation: The route is depleted, the map gives no useful pallet or the Killer has already cleared the area.
rows.action: Leave the resource plan and take the best remaining chase path, generator or rescue job instead of travelling back to defend an exhausted tile.
rows.why: The strategy wins by avoiding dead zones, not by maintaining a route that no longer exists.

abortWhen: Abort a reset when the Killer can reach you before it completes or when the restored pallet does not protect a useful route.
Stop routing around a spent area when ordinary objective or rescue work now repays more team tempo.

soloQ: Treat a reset as your own timing decision and return to the next job when no teammate is visibly using the recovered route.
coordinatedSwf: Call the pallet area being spent or reset, then release the assignment so another player can keep the next generator or rescue covered.

strengths: Avoid dead zones and waste fewer pallets when the map supplies a usable route.
weaknesses: Map RNG and rapid Killer resource destruction can remove the activation path.
A reset interaction and a pallet drop both spend time or exposure that may not be repaid.
killerCounterplay: The Killer can clear resources quickly, refuse the expected pallet interaction or change timing so a reset becomes unsafe.
commonMistakes: Dropping a pallet for the perk trigger without planning the next route.
Starting a reset while the Killer can interrupt it or while another job is more urgent.
Treating Five Moves Ahead as window information or Alert as a complete resource map.

related.why: This is a pallet-economy specialization of the broader chase and looping strategy.
Fragile-Pallet Restoration is the narrower chest-to-pallet branch and should be treated as a setup-dependent addition, not a normal pallet reset.
